title: Comparing corneal biomechanic changes among solo cataract surgery, microhook ab interno trabeculotomy and iStent implantation

indication: open-angle glaucoma (mostly POAG; some exfoliation and one steroid-induced glaucoma) for the combined angle-surgery groups; cataract in eyes without glaucoma for the solo-cataract group

groups.indication: open-angle glaucoma (51 POAG, 1 exfoliation glaucoma, 1 steroid-induced glaucoma; Results)
groups.description: cataract surgery combined with microhook ab interno trabeculotomy (two quadrants); 53 eyes of 36 patients

groups.indication: open-angle glaucoma (56 POAG, 3 exfoliation glaucoma; Results)
groups.description: cataract surgery combined with iStent implantation into the nasal angle; 59 eyes of 37 patients

groups.indication: cataract in eyes without glaucoma or other ocular disease (normal eyes)
groups.description: phacoemulsification with intraocular lens implantation alone; 62 eyes of 42 patients

exclusions.reason: no absolute follow-up values (baseline only, follow-up only as model-estimated changes); same eyes as the GAT series

exclusions.what: Corvis ST and ORA biomechanical parameters (CH, CCT, A1/A2, SP-A1, SSI and others)

notes: Medication: eye drop score at baseline, 3 and 6 months is tabulated for the two glaucoma groups (Table 2 rows 4-6); not extracted (no medication series in schema 1.0.0).

Group roles: microhook trabeculotomy and iStent are two standard techniques compared without an investigational arm; solo cataract surgery in non-glaucoma eyes is the study's control group; all are role control.
Patients contributed one or two eyes; the study's p-values come from linear mixed models with the patient as a random effect.
